E1.evidence: Issue #262 asks for the header rename ("the suffix of header files should be changed from *.h to *.hpp"), and a commenter anticipates the downstream break: "renaming the header files will create a problem on other packages that depends on this package." (https://github.com/ros-perception/vision_opencv/issues/262#issuecomment-629760429). The vision_opencv maintainer confirms the removal: "All .h files have been deprecated in I-turtle, and have removed for J-turtle onwards!" (https://github.com/ros-perception/vision_opencv/issues/262#issuecomment-1760609581), done in PR #517 / commit 5d6148ab "remove header files that were deprecated in I-turtle". The Autoware maintainer's fix PR #11873 "fix: add cv_bridge.hpp support", filed under the Jazzy-support tracking issue, replaces the consumer's include: "-#include <cv_bridge/cv_bridge.h>" / "+#include <cv_bridge/cv_bridge.hpp>  // for ROS 2 Jazzy or newer" (https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/11873/files). This is a maintainer-confirmed consumer/provider mismatch; there is no reproducer or error log.

E2.evidence: Provider cv_bridge removed the header cv_bridge/cv_bridge.h (commit 5d6148ab834e380ee0aea1a15d193b860dba8acf: "cv_bridge/include/cv_bridge/cv_bridge.h removed"; tag 4.0.0 and later contain only cv_bridge.hpp). The consumer autoware_traffic_light_visualization at e274c98f still includes the removed header in src/traffic_light_roi_visualizer/shape_draw.hpp: "#include <cv_bridge/cv_bridge.h>". The resolving edit changes the consumer's reference to the provider's declared header, i.e. follows a provider interface change; it is not a deployment name binding or a build-system-only change.

E3.evidence: UPGRADE: the consumer references cv_bridge.h as it existed up to the Humble release of cv_bridge (3.2.1, which ships only cv_bridge.h), while the Jazzy provider (4.1.0) no longer has it. The fix's own comments mark the two sides: "#include <cv_bridge/cv_bridge.hpp>  // for ROS 2 Jazzy or newer" / "#include <cv_bridge/cv_bridge.h>  // for ROS 2 Humble or older" (https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/11873/files).

E4.evidence: Code-level statements of the mismatch by maintainers: the provider-side removal statement ("have removed for J-turtle onwards!", https://github.com/ros-perception/vision_opencv/issues/262#issuecomment-1760609581) and the consumer-side fix commit f50b5c3991d3e6d4591d97fd60c51df4deed116a "fix: add cv_bridge.hpp support (#11873)". No compile error for this package is shown in the sources (the Jazzy build status in https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/issues/11418#issuecomment-3757294247 is an unattributed pie chart), so the effect is undocumented.

resolution.summary: Consumer includes the provider's .hpp header when present and falls back to .h otherwise: "+#if __has_include(<cv_bridge/cv_bridge.hpp>)" / "+#include <cv_bridge/cv_bridge.hpp>  // for ROS 2 Jazzy or newer" / "+#else" / "+#include <cv_bridge/cv_bridge.h>  // for ROS 2 Humble or older" / "+#endif" in perception/autoware_traffic_light_visualization/src/traffic_light_roi_visualizer/shape_draw.hpp (https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/11873/files). cv_bridge unchanged.

(https://github.com/autowarefoundation/autoware_universe/pull/11873); consumer at PR head 59bd3d1242446ec4068d0b3bff6ab35a61ee13cc (merged as f50b5c39). The provider is identified by distro only; Jazzy carried a single vision_opencv release (4.1.0-1) on that date, so the provider revision is 4.1.0 by the rosdistro record rather than by the PR's own words.

notes: Issue #262 itself reports no failure; it asks for the ROS 2 migration-guide header naming. Its fix (vision_opencv PR #448, merge fa5213bb1cb2ab63fa7648a3e1b7c480f622b54c, 2022-09-10) added .hpp headers and turned the .h headers into deprecation shims ("+#warning This header is obsolete, please include cv_bridge/rgb_colors.hpp instead"); in the Iron release (3.3.0 and the iron branch) the same consumer include would therefore have compiled with a deprecation warning (a warning_only composition, not observed in the sources). The removal came later in PR #517 / 5d6148ab (2023-10-12), first released in 4.0.0. Other consumers fixed by the same Autoware PR (not specified here): autoware_tensorrt_vad (lib/synchronization_strategy.cpp, src/vad_node.cpp, src/vad_node.hpp), autoware_tensorrt_bevdet (bevdet_node.hpp), autoware_tensorrt_bevformer (bevformer_node.hpp). In the chosen consumer, node.hpp already carried the __has_include guard at the broken revision, so shape_draw.hpp was the only remaining .h include. The same removal also dropped cv_bridge/rgb_colors.h and image_geometry's pinhole_camera_model.h / stereo_camera_model.h (not used by this consumer). Canonical-form note: the header include paths cv_bridge/cv_bridge.h and cv_bridge/cv_bridge.hpp are recorded with the api: form because no canonical form exists for a C++ header; the removed element is the header, while the C++ symbols it declared (CvImagePtr, toCvCopy, Exception) remain available under cv_bridge.hpp. consumer_built_against basis: broken is inferred (the consumer's include of cv_bridge/cv_bridge.h matches the Humble release 3.2.1 from humble/distribution.yaml on 2026-01-15, "version: 3.2.1-1", and the fix labels the .h include "for ROS 2 Humble or older"); resolved 4.1.0 follows from "Compiles locally with jazzy" and the Jazzy distribution pin.
